::: {#thm-permutation-p-valid}
#### The permutation p-value is valid

Let $Y = (\Outvar_1, \ldots, \Outvar_n)$ be exchangeable under $H_0$ (@def-exchangeable),
and let $p_{\text{perm}}$ be the [permutation p-value](#def-permutation-p-value) of $T(Y)$.
Then $p_{\text{perm}}$ is a [valid p-value](multiple-testing.qmd#def-valid-p-value):

$$\Pr_{H_0}\paren{p_{\text{perm}} \le u} \le u \quad \text{for every } u \in [0, 1].$$

:::

::: proof

Since $p_{\text{perm}} = N_\iota(Y) / n!$ takes values in multiples of $1 / n!$,
it is enough to take $u = k / n!$ for an integer $k$ with $0 \le k \le n!$:
for other $u$ the event $\set{p_{\text{perm}} \le u}$ equals the event for $\floor{u \, n!} / n!$, which is at most $u$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_{H_0}\paren{p_{\text{perm}} \le \frac{k}{n!}}
&= \Pr_{H_0}\paren{N_\iota(Y) \le k}
&& \text{(multiply the inequality by $n!$)}\\
&= \Pr_{H_0}\paren{N_\iota(Y_\sigma) \le k}
&& \text{(for each $\sigma$, $Y_\sigma$ has the distribution of $Y$, by exchangeability)}\\
&= \Pr_{H_0}\paren{N_\sigma(Y) \le k}
&& \text{(relabeling identity)}\\
&= \E{\indic{N_\sigma(Y) \le k}}
&& \text{(probability of an event is the expected value of its indicator)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \E{\indic{N_\sigma(Y) \le k}}
&& \text{(the average of $n!$ equal terms)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n!} \E{\sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \indic{N_\sigma(Y) \le k}}
&& \text{(expectation of a sum is the sum of expectations)}\\
&\le \frac{1}{n!} \E{k}
&& \text{(counting bound, with $N = n!$ and $t_\sigma = T(Y_\sigma)$)}\\
&= \frac{k}{n!}
&& \text{(the expected value of a constant is the constant)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The justifications of the third and the seventh line are @lem-relabeling-count and @lem-top-k-count.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-permutation-p-valid}
#### Validity in a small simulation

Simulate $10^4$ data sets of 6 independent standard Gaussian values, three per group,
so that $H_0$ holds,
and compute the exact permutation p-value of $\abs{\bar \outvar_1 - \bar y_2}$ for each:

```{r}
#| label: permutation-p-valid
#| code-fold: false
set.seed(580)
group1_choices <- combn(6, 3)
exact_p <- replicate(1e4, {
  y <- rnorm(6)
  stats <- apply(group1_choices, 2, function(idx) {
    in1 <- 1:6 %in% idx
    abs(mean(y[in1]) - mean(y[!in1]))
  })
  mean(round(stats, 10) >= round(stats[1], 10))
})
u <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5)
data.frame(
  u = u,
  fraction_p_at_most_u = sapply(u, function(x) mean(exact_p <= x))
)
```

Each fraction is close to its $u$, within simulation error.
Here the exact p-value takes the values $0.1, 0.2, \ldots, 1$ with equal probability,
because the 20 statistics form 10 mirror pairs with no other ties,
so @thm-permutation-p-valid holds with equality.
:::
